text:
anya: heads up — seeing a bump in `invoke_errors` around 23:48 UTC. console shows a bunch of toolcall rejects that look like they should've passed. sample attached below.

sam: can you paste the tool output and the validator error?

anya: here's the tool payload and the validator log we get from the adapter: 
```json
{"choice": {"text": "OK", "debug_info": {"trace_id": "abc123"}}}
```
validator log: `schema-gate: reject - unexpected_property 'debug_info' in /choice`

jonah: hmm — the tool is returning an extra `debug_info` object we don't care about. our validator is running strict mode for tool responses which rejects unknown fields. that will trigger fallback routing.

maria: fallback routing means requests hit the fallback model and double-run in some cases, right? that's going to inflate token cost and affect quotas for customers using dedicated capacity. :grimacing:

anya: exact. saw a customer spike in usage that correlates with the rejects window. infra-bot also fired an alert: `invoke-fallback-rate +18%`

infra-bot: ALERT: invoke-fallback-rate exceeded threshold on prod (23:49 UTC). count=128 over 5m.

sam: proposal: add a short-lived canary change that sets `validator.mode=permissive` for tool outputs for 10% of traffic and ensure permissive still enforces core required fields. that way we avoid wholesale disabling.

jonah: agree, but let's avoid touching the global validator. we can add a routing flag `allow_extra_props=true` on the 'tool' route layer and only for that model/fleet. prevents coupling validator changes to other routes.

anya: putting a concrete canary config here — will test in prod-canary namespace: 
```yaml
routes:
  - name: tool-invoke-canary
    match: route == "tool"
    percentage: 10
    validator_overrides:
      mode: permissive
      allow_unknown_properties: true
```

maria: we also need telemetry. current metrics just show `invoke_rejects` count. add a sampled `raw_tool_output` log for 0.1% of rejects so we can audit what fields show up without storing everything.

sam: +1. also we should add a dashboard tile in console: "Toolcall Rejects by validator reason" with a breakdown (unknown_field, missing_required, invalid_type). helps ops quickly triage.

jonah: caveat: permissive mode could hide real schema regressions (missing required fields) if we aren't careful. make sure canonical required field checks still run even in permissive mode. only skip unknown-property rejection.

anya: plan: 1) deploy route flag canary (10%) 2) enable sampled raw output telemetry (0.1%) 3) update dashboard tile 4) monitor cost signals for 2h -> rollback if fallback rate or token spend worsens. I'll own rollout.

maria: timeline? need signoff from finance if we expect >5% cost delta.

anya: can do the canary now, will run for 2h and post a short cost estimate before enabling.

sam: I'll PR the validator change and the route flag. small unit tests to show required fields still validated. ping me once canary is live and I'll set up the dashboard panel.

jonah: add an internal note in the runbook: when hits come from tool adapters add `allow_extra_props` instead of changing validator globally. avoids accidental laxity on consumer endpoints.

maria: approved to proceed with canary as long as cost monitoring is on and finance is notified.

anya: starting canary now, will report status in 15m. :rocket:

infra-bot: DEPLOY: route-config update to prod-canary triggered by anya at 23:51 UTC. change-id=cfg-4829

sam: thanks — once we have a few samples from telemetry we'll decide if we widen to 50% or revert.

anya: quick live sample from the `raw_tool_output` stream (sanitized): 
```
{"choice": {"text": "OK", "extra_debug": "stack=...", "meta": {"version":"1.2.3"}}}
```
jonah: looks safe. not seeing missing required keys.

maria: keeping an eye on quota dashboards, alert if token spend > +7% vs baseline.

anya: canary at 10% stable for 20m. invoke_rejects down ~82% and fallback-rate down ~70%. cost delta ~= +1.8% so far.

sam: excellent. open a follow-up to add `allow_extra_props` as a first-class route-level flag and document in the config reference.

anya: will do. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
